incidents.summary: The CMA opened an investigation into whether Trainline included mandatory booking fees in upfront prices displayed on its app and website.

sources.title: Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School investigated for drip pricing - GOV.UK
sources.quote: Trainline: being investigated over whether all mandatory fees have been included in the upfront prices displayed to consumers buying train and coach tickets in advance on the Trainline app and website.

sources.title: Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School investigated for drip pricing - GOV.UK
sources.quote: For train travel, the CMA observed transactions with fees ranging from £0.59 to £2.79. For coach bookings, it was a £1.50 booking fee.

incidents.summary: The ASA upheld a complaint that Trainline's TV and radio lowest-price claims were misleading, and Trainline said the discontinued adverts would not run again.

sources.title: Rail ticket price claims in Trainline ads were ‘misleading’ – watchdog
sources.quote: The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) ruled a TV ad with a robot on a fictional planet stating: “You won’t find cheaper same-day tickets anywhere else” breached broadcasting rules.

sources.title: Rail ticket price claims in Trainline ads were ‘misleading’ – watchdog
sources.quote: It made the same assessment in relation to a radio ad featuring a man engaged in an archaeological dig, claiming: “We won’t find cheaper tickets anywhere else”.

sources.title: Rail ticket price claims in Trainline ads were ‘misleading’ – watchdog
sources.quote: Trainline told the ASA it had no plans to re-air either of the ads, and future ads would not feature the claim “you won’t find cheaper”.

positives: Trainline added railcard-invalidity warnings to its iOS and Android apps and website.
SBTi validated Trainline's net-zero-by-2040 target and its near-term target to reduce absolute scope 1 and 2 emissions by 55.2% by 2030.
